q: Does a solar powered cold room really cut emissions?
title: Solar cold rooms for farm produce
short: Yes, against a grid or diesel powered cold room, because the cooling electricity comes from the panels. Two things still count: refrigerant leaks, which are Scope 1 at the gas GWP, and backup power. The embodied emissions of panels and batteries go in Scope 3 capital goods in the year bought.
audience: FPOs, aggregators and cold chain startups

ul: Solar generation and any grid or diesel backup.
Produce stored per month, for per tonne figures.

p: Less spoiled produce means less food wasted, but report that separately from the energy saving and do not net it off.

senseible: Senseible reads fuel invoices and electricity bills and applies IPCC 2006 factors and the CEA grid factor (0.710 kg CO2 per kWh), so you can compare Scope 1 and 2 before and after a change from the documents themselves.
